facts: The paper 'Is parents’ employment uncertainty linked to children's development? Analysing patterns and mechanisms in France' was authored by Marta Facchini, Lidia Panico, and Carlo Barone, and published in the European Sociological Review on 2026-10-29 (doi:10.1093/esr/jcag042).

The study examines how household employment uncertainty (HEU)—defined to include temporary employment and unemployment—relates to children's cognitive, socio-emotional, and physical development in France.
Data were drawn from four waves of the nationally representative French Longitudinal Study of Children (ELFE).
Methodologically, the authors used ordinary least squares (OLS) and linear probability models alongside counterfactual mediation analysis and regression-with-residuals.
Accumulation and persistence of HEU within households were found to be associated with lower cognitive development of up to −0.2 standard deviations (SD) at ages 2 and 3.5.
Results for children's socio-emotional development were less robust, and physical health showed no correlation with HEU, possibly buffered by comprehensive healthcare.

Counterfactual mediation analysis revealed that income and parental investment in cognitively-enhancing activities mediate cognitive outcomes, whereas parental stress mediates socio-emotional outcomes.
The authors conclude that household employment uncertainty represents an important pathway in early social inequality, warranting targeted policy interventions.
